method: Independently reviewed all40 fixed mixed-order candidate sheets against all six initial references and seven unanimously accepted pilot references. Only a specific coat/anatomy match is accepted. Neither predicted slot names nor other reviewers current decisions were opened before freezing. No backfill or inference.
disclosure: AI-assisted visual comparison, not external human farmer or owner ground truth. Initial labels are the existing pilot reference convention.
Prior scene and pilot ordering exposure are known; these40 questions are deterministically mixed and their expected-name manifest has not been opened by this reviewer before freezing.
The seven additional pilot references were accepted by all three reviewers in the earlier frozen comparison. The five uncertain pilot photos were not used as references or replaced.
Small/changed views remain uncertain even when a likely animal could be guessed. The known list has only six cows; unlisted cows may resemble them.
No encoder outputs, similarities, ground-truth metrics or other remaining-photo reviewer conclusions were consulted.

rows.reason: Narrow white shoulder collar, small separated middle fleck and split far-end marking on a mainly dark body match initial 2 and pilot P02/P03.
Two separated irregular white shoulder/rump islands on the dark torso match initial 6 and P10/P11; neck is bent but the coat regions remain coherent.
A smaller triangular shoulder island and larger notched rump island are separated by a long dark region, consistent with initial 6 and the accepted side views.
Distinct isolated white patches at shoulder and rump, with dark coat between and no collar, match initial 6; context supports one foreground-left animal.
White forward and rear regions surround the broad dark middle saddle; the dark island on the pale rear matches initial 1 and both accepted pilot views despite the bent neck.
The pale shoulder triangle and separate rear white island, with a long unbroken black middle, match the accepted cow6 views; context contains one isolated body.

A side view shows white ends and large dark flank regions, but the relevant curled initial reference hides this side. The pattern is not uniquely linked to a known animal; posture and generic color layout alone are insufficient.

A mostly pale side with a dark central patch is visible, but the same-side correspondence to curled initial4 is unclear. Neither the broad colors nor feeder location establish a unique identity.
The broad central dark saddle and pale rump with a separate dark terminal island match initial1 and both accepted pilot examples; the foreground is one animal.

The curled dark body retains the distinctive broad white lower flank with separate dark islands/notches seen in initial5, plus the small pale upper shoulder fleck. This near-matching pose provides direct coat correspondence absent from the uncertain later standing views.

Bent pose still reveals the pale shoulder belt with a small adjacent island and the split rear marking of initial2; it differs from reference6's two isolated broader islands.
Thin shoulder collar, small upper-body fleck and divided rear white marking on a dark back match initial2 and P02/P03.

The black curled trunk, broad pale lower flank with dark islands/notches, small upper white fleck and bent head agree with initial5 in a comparable pose.

The white spotted crop lacks much head/neck context and presents a different top-side pattern from the confirmed lateral cow3 images. A likely resemblance is not sufficient for a unique biological assignment.
A sharply turned white-and-black torso exposes a side not established by the curled initial reference. Neighboring feeder animals and changed posture make exact coat correspondence uncertain.

Comparable curled pose to initial4 shows the broad pale rear, dark middle with a small isolated pale mark and branching pale lower-flank pattern. These matching internal markings support4 rather than merely a black/white body class.
